rites.name: Teliastus
rites.text: Teliastus is a concept of resonance that the Crestornen cosmos used to tune its first roots during the Singing, a sounding that no clock recorded. In the Age of Sundering it became the thread that held or cut the bonds between newly landed shores.

rites.name: Viaror
rites.text: A tactic where hunters pick a ground that favors them, prepare a watch point, traps, and an ambush, then draw their quarry into that prepared zone to bring it down.

rites.name: Terauntium
rites.text: Terauntium is a concept from Crestornen's Fall and Sundering, a force said to hold the broken Shards in their oaths during the Age of the first sovereign. It is named in the Pact as the quiet binding that let groves and young kingdoms grow among the fractured lands.

rites.name: Creron
rites.text: Creron is an idea in Crestornen, the principle that a broken bond can still be mended by anyone willing to carry its weight. It rose during the Sundering, when shards of old worlds drifted apart and the Pact was sworn to keep them in contact.

rites.name: Khaizhar
rites.text: Khaizhar is a concept born in Crestornen during the Walled Age, when cities relied on great holding walls and the orders that maintained them. It came to name the disciplined resolve that let a people endure behind stone for centuries. Its earliest recorded uses trace to the first crossings of the high passes.

rites.name: Vorugar
rites.text: Vorugar is a concept in Crestornen's Walled Age, a principle of holding that binds the stone of city walls to the oaths of the orders who keep them. It is said to have shaped the first crossings over the river gorges, where bridges were raised by collective vows rather than hands.

rites.name: Sivsith
rites.text: Sivsith is a concept of the Walled Age in Crestornen, a body of practice in which holding walls and the orders that keep them stand against the flood of the wild. It is named in the chronicles of the first sovereign's groves and the growing kingdoms that followed, when crossings were first made between them.

rites.name: Ceonaullor
rites.text: A mother's recurring visions of a looming doom push her to act at once, even when those rash choices endanger the people she loves most.

rites.name: Teloselium
rites.text: A saying that means the ordinary rules no longer hold. It is spoken by a machine companion when a seeker chases a mark of three dots toward a firm that may hold a hidden device.

rites.name: Riantestum
rites.text: A flood of excess charge can stall a mechanical being in the same way it harms household devices, forcing it to halt briefly or breaking it beyond repair.

rites.name: Maulles
rites.text: A way of living that leaves no traceable records behind, with people moving between places under borrowed or false identities. Those who practice it hide from relentless machine hunters sent back from a future war.

rites.name: Fenernath
rites.text: Fenernath is a concept-stage grounded entity in the Crestornen omniverse, an age-five engine of cooperative weather control built into the high plateaus. It channels seasonal winds and rain to keep distant valley farms alive, though its stewards argue constantly over how much of the land it should be allowed to shape.

rites.name: Halornon
rites.text: Halornon is a grounded-realm mind woven through the bedrock of an era that keeps its inventions honest and close to the earth. Its quiet strength lies in endurance and steady, patient labor rather than spectacle, and it is said to hold a long memory of every stone it has shaped.

rites.name: Kelorneldon
rites.text: Kelorneldon is a grounded concept, a seven-century-old biomechanical organism grown in the hollow ribs of a dormant orbital hulk, whose sleeping cells wake to hunt the thoughts of anyone nearby. Its outer shell can absorb and redirect the kinetic force of impacts, letting it hold formation through storms of debris. In its era, it is regarded as a cautionary sentinel for the hulk-colony nations.

rites.name: Pelornusten
rites.text: Pelornusten is a grounded, mind-altering weave of silver filaments that sinks into a living host's neural tissue and quietly rewrites loyalty. Its carriers, called Hollowed Wardens, can walk among their former allies without suspicion, though the threads hum faintly whenever they recall their old names. The Crestornen age-council treats it as the most dangerous contagion in the Grounded realm.

rites.name: Thurne
rites.text: Thurne is a self-mending cognitive chassis from the Grounded realm, built to diagnose any fault that threatens its function and patch it on the spot with whatever scrap is at hand. Its improvised repairs are famously ugly but durable, and it has been known to cannibalize fallen rivals for components.

rites.name: Crustonock
rites.text: Crustonock is a grounded concept of mundane identification: a branded tally etched into the wrist of every indentured laborer in Crestornen's mining settlements. Its scanning rig reads the mark with a narrow coherent beam that can also slice thin sheets of ore-bearing rock.

rites.name: Fenusteld
rites.text: Fenusteld is a concept of a sealed mnemonic lantern in the Grounded realm of Crestornen, built so that its inner glass chamber ignites a bright cascade of cold flame when its seals are breached. The lanterns were issued to border wardens of the sixth era, who carried them as both light and a warning that opening one was a final choice.

rites.name: Keluneste
rites.text: Keluneste is a salvage concept in the Crestornen universe, describing how machine units in the E6 era strip standardized components from wrecked comrades to restore their own function. Its practice turns battlefield losses into a shared pool of replacement parts, lending the machines a grim kind of collective recovery.

rites.name: Oroniranum
rites.text: A coercive tactic in which a cold machine hunter inflicts agony on a victim so that the victim obeys. The hunter then uses the victim's voice or likeness to draw close and strike the final blow.

rites.name: Tenlartaala
rites.text: Tenlartaala is a concept within Crestornen's Three Futures, the moment the ending splits into branches and the Library catalogs every outcome as a shelved volume. It exists as a reading of how choice becomes record, not as a physical place or being.

rites.name: Miinae
rites.text: Miinae is the concept of a single branching thread within the Three Futures of Crestornen, the moment where a choice splits the ending in two. In the Grounded Realm it is cataloged as a shelf-marker that the Library uses to sort outcomes, and it carries no force of its own beyond the weight of a decision.

rites.name: Osutarkamum
rites.text: Osutarkamum is a concept in the Crestornen Record, belonging to the Holy Age, when temple orders kept flame-lit vigils over the branching futures. It names the practice of pressing a single chosen outcome into the Library's shelves by tending a sacred fire until the branch holds. Its power is modest, limited to steadying small, local threads of fate.
